view_attestation.method: Whole viewed once, then each supplied half once, followed by one enlarged crop per remaining grouped locus. The opposite-direction lines were read upright only in their individual rotated crops. No OCR, no external source, no other scan or reader file, and no delegation. No settled target was recropped.

differences.location: U1, numerator of the last quotient
differences.evidence: The primed Q is the first letter after the minus; the following letter has the upright stem and upper loop of P. Read on half a, without a crop.

differences.location: U2, overwritten predecessor between P-double-prime/Q and 2
differences.evidence: A dense horizontal group has a short vertical projection below it. The predecessor remains a supported plus candidate; its complete strokes cannot be separated.
A short rightward horizontal extension is clear; the crowded vertical ink may belong to the overwritten predecessor. Minus remains primary, plus remains an alternative.
A narrow curved downstroke and hooked foot protrude immediately left of P, across older opposite-direction writing. The candidate 2 remains unresolved.
The plus, the P with an upper right loop, and the open left parenthesis are visible. The writing stops after that parenthesis; there is no terminal comma.

differences.location: U3, logarithmic quotients, including first denominator correction
differences.evidence: The old denominator has a full oval and descending right tail; the live P has a straight stem and upper right bowl. Both quotient bars, the central minus, and the second Q denominator are legible.

The raised mark has a joined bent top and descending right end. A 2-like form remains primary; touching prime strokes remain possible. H’s primary double-prime reading survives as the alternative, so this is a qualified disagreement.
Two raised strokes meet in a low bend above the x. Their joining prevents removal of the x-squared alternative; x-double-prime remains primary and agrees with H’s candidate.

differences.location: U4, prime on the middle y
differences.evidence: A short raised stroke lies above/right of y but coincides with opposite-direction ink. A prime remains the supported candidate without a secure separation of the layers.

differences.location: U4, exponent on the final y
differences.evidence: The crowded raised area contains more than one small stroke; the opposite-direction f and subscript pass through it. Double prime remains primary and single prime remains possible.

differences.location: Between U3 and the opposing prose: detached point
differences.evidence: A small compact dark point is visible at approximately (969,601), separated from the surrounding characters. Its layer, hand and function cannot be assigned from these views; the point shape alone is preserved.
A capital-like upright and upper bowl survive above the live looped f, with a separate raised hook at the right. P-prime remains supported, but the overtracing prevents confident separation.

differences.location: U6, expanded quotient-rule display, unambiguous structure and terms
differences.evidence: The opening and closing parentheses, both crossed P-prime Q-prime products, the Q-double-prime P product, the subtraction of the parenthesized P-prime Q minus Q-prime P product, and 2 times a separately slashed Q followed by Q-prime are all visible. The long fraction rule is present. Separate rows record the crowded signs, the first Q-squared state and denominator.

notes: Two overlapping handwritten orientations occupy the sheet. The opposite-direction calculation is crossed by two long diagonals; this overall cancellation is already described by H and is not counted as an H difference.

H’s introductory note and the captions naming the two layers are apparatus. Its descriptive sur f=P/Q is not treated as an extra manuscript formula. H’s page{5} identifies its transcription page; no manuscript page number or title/date is supplied here. The pencilled archive 5 is recorded as a comment.

No explicit verbal statement of author uncertainty occurs. Unfinished written expressions are retained: P( on the second upright line, the lowest 2p²Q²(-Q-prime/Q+ fragment, and the last half-turned range 2≤i≤ with no upper bound.

Mathematical attention drew scrutiny to the product exponent, coefficient signs, the Q-squared cancellation state and the prose indices. No expected identity was used to replace the ink. In particular the primary product superscript remains 2-like and the prose retains e(d-1), f(d-2).

The first factor Q-squared in the expanded numerator is crossed where the older long diagonal runs; the timing and local cancellation state cannot be recovered confidently. A live primary reading and the cancelled-Q alternative are both preserved.
The short second stroke along the right-hand fraction rule is drawn separately. Its intention is not assigned. The detached point at (969,601) is preserved separately with uncertain role and hand.

C doubt rows are based on actual unsure markers, not the supplied notation/abbreviation table. All 25 actual C uncertainty loci are logged. Resolving a C doubt sets diff_C=true even when its primary candidate is kept.

Some local rows lie within a larger H omission, notably the expanded quotient-rule fraction and lowest fragment. Their overlap is explicit; they should not be counted as independent missing whole displays.

The r05 prose crop includes the whole wording but reaches the top of the overlapping ascender at the overwritten second-list-item letter. The supplied halves had already shown that region; the doubtful predecessor is retained, and no recrop was made.
The manuscript’s exact abbreviations comb. lin, coeff, etc are retained. There is no expansion in reading.tex.
